candidates.excerpt: Weekly traffic on U.S.railroads was 534,256 carloads and intermodal units for the week ending Oct. 10, up 7.2 percent compared with the same week a year ago. Carload commodities totaled 232,004 carloads, up 3.4 percent, according to Association of American Railroads data, while intermodal volume was 302,252 containers and trailers, up 10.4% y/y. Eight of 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase from the same week in 2025. They were topped by metallic ores and metals typically used in steelmaking, 19.7%; forest products, 9.6%, and motor vehicles and parts, 9.4%. Declines were seen in coal, 2%, and farm products excluding grain and food, 5.6%. For the first 40 weeks of this year, U.S. railroads reported cumulative volume of 9,142,597 carloads, up 2.7%, and 11,379,949 intermodal units, up 4.4% from a year ago. candidates.title: Hamann, Union Pacific chief financial officer, to retire
candidates.excerpt: OMAHA, Neb. — Chief Financial Officer Jennifer Hamann will retire in early 2027, Union Pacific has announced. Hamann, who joined Union Pacific in 1992, was named CFO in January 2020. She had previously held leadership roles in a broad range of areas, including finance, human resources, marketing and sales, investor relations, and corporate audit. “For 35 years, she led with integrity and heart, guiding our finances through historic challenges, executing our strategy, mentoring future leaders and representing Union Pacific across the industry,” UP CEO Jim Vena said in a press release. “Jennifer was tough — she never said yes unless she believed it was the right thing to do for Union Pacific. She made this railroad stronger, and her contributions will be felt for generations. I am deeply grateful for her leadership and friendship.” Hamann is the first woman to serve as the railroad’s chief financial officer. candidates.title: UK ports hit back at Brussels over ETS diversion claims
candidates.excerpt: UK ports hit back at Brussels over ETS diversion claims British ports have challenged European Union claims that shipping lines are diverting container traffic to the UK to escape carbon charges, warning that proposed anti-evasion measures risk penalising billions of pounds of investment in British terminals. The British Ports Association (BPA) has rejected findings from Spain’s EU ETS Observatory linking rising UK container activity to the bloc’s Emissions Trading System, arguing that new capacity, changing liner networks and commercial competition offer more convincing explanations. In a new report, the association said around 85% of the UK’s container traffic growth in 2025 was concentrated in London, following the opening of DP World’s £350m ($465m) fourth berth at London Gateway in late 2024. candidates.title: HMM commits $1.6bn to 12 more containerships
candidates.excerpt: South Korea’s HMM is pressing ahead with its fleet expansion programme, approving a $1.62bn investment in 12 containerships comprising eight 13,000 teu newbuildings and four smaller vessels. The Seoul-listed carrier’s board approved spending KRW2.168trn ($1.617bn) yesterday, according to a stock exchange filing. The investment includes fresh orders for eight 13,000 teu ships, alongside the acquisition of three 2,800 teu vessels and one 1,700 teu ship through resale transactions involving newbuildings already under construction. The 12 vessels will add a combined 114,100 teu of capacity, with deliveries scheduled to be completed by December 2029. HMM has yet to identify the shipyards responsible for the eight larger vessels or the sellers of the four smaller ships. Propulsion specifications have also not been disclosed. The vessels were each hit by unknown projectiles and were not identified in the warning notices, but Vanguard Tech has identified the container ships as GFS Pride, GFS Giselle, and Al Saadiyat and the tanker as Alfonso. The four attacks bring UKMTO’s tally of warnings to 24 for the month of October to date, as well as three advisories. Maritime & Port Authority of Singapore (MPA) confirmed that Singapore-flagged GFS Pride has sunk since a projectile strike caused damage and a fire onboard. All 21 crew were safely evacuated, it added. Vanguard Tech said GFS Giselle suffered minor damage after being struck during its inbound transit before continuing on its way with no injuries reported; MPA confirmed the 22 crew were safe and that the ship has arrived at safe anchorage despite sustaining hull damage.
